chunks: Al-Saffar from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammam from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said:

Abbad ibn Abdillah al-Basri asked him about a man who made a vow to God to walk to His Sacred House, so he walked half the way, or less, or more. He said: He looks at what he spent from that point onward and gives it in charity.
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a vow to walk to Mecca if one stops halfway?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the expiation for a vow to perform Hajj on foot when interrupted, ruling that the individual must give in charity the value of the expenses incurred up to the point of stopping. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the financial burden of the vow is proportional to the actual resources consumed rather than a fixed penalty, distinguishing it from general kaffarah. It underscores the importance of intention and actual expenditure in fulfilling religious vows (nadhr) within the framework of fiqh.
